title: A Survey of Reinforcement Learning for Large Reasoning Models
version: v3, 2025-10-09 (arXiv page says last revised 9 Oct 2025)
actual_read_scope: Read the complete arXiv v3 PDF text (120 pages) and its reference list. Focused synthesis: Sections 2.1-2.2, 3.1.1-3.1.5, 3.2.5, 3.3.1-3.3.2, 4.1-4.5, 5.1, and 7.4. No cited paper was independently read.

routes.problem: Sparse outcome rewards make long reasoning chains hard to assign credit to and can encourage reward hacking or unfaithful traces.
routes.mechanism: Use rule-based verifiers for correctness/format, generative verifiers for semantic or open-ended judging, and process/token/step/turn rewards to shorten the credit-assignment horizon.
routes.inference_token_connection: Indirect-to-direct: process supervision may teach better reasoning trajectories, but the survey does not establish a generally lower inference-token Pareto frontier. Explicit length penalties and adaptive length rewards are direct token-cost routes.
routes.notes: Dense rewards are described as improving training efficiency/stability and credit assignment; inference efficiency is a separate question.

routes.problem: Group/sequence rewards have high variance and may optimize Pass@1 while collapsing exploration and Pass@K diversity.
routes.mechanism: GRPO-style group baselines, leave-one-out/ranking baselines, and Pass@K-aligned objectives redistribute set-level credit to individual samples.
routes.inference_token_connection: Indirect: exploration diversity can change the quality of reasoning candidates at a fixed inference budget; no direct token reduction is established by the survey.
routes.notes: The survey reports conflicting Pass@1/Pass@K behavior and treats exploration collapse as an unresolved issue.

routes.problem: Uniform rollout sampling wastes training compute on mastered, impossible, all-correct, or all-wrong prompts.
routes.mechanism: Online filtering, failure-rate prioritization, difficulty estimation, curriculum schedules, rollout replay, adaptive batch sizing, and category/item-level controllers concentrate rollouts on informative prompts.
routes.inference_token_connection: Training-sampling efficiency only: fewer wasted rollouts/tokens per policy update; it is not evidence that the trained model answers with fewer inference tokens.
routes.notes: The survey explicitly frames these methods as learning efficiency and rollout budget allocation.

routes.problem: Long-chain RL rollouts are expensive and repeated prefixes duplicate KV-cache work.
routes.mechanism: Tree/MCTS rollouts, shared-prefix or segment-wise sampling, branch-point selection, and node-level process rewards reuse partial computation and provide finer credit.
routes.inference_token_connection: Primarily RL training sampling efficiency/compute-only. Shared prefixes can reduce training GPU hours; the survey does not show reduced final answer tokens. Tree-based inference may spend more tokens if used at test time.
routes.notes: Do not conflate cheaper rollout generation with token-efficient final inference.

routes.problem: Long reasoning traces improve accuracy but raise inference cost and can overthink easy instances.
routes.mechanism: Length-aware/adaptive reward shaping, relative-length regularization, difficulty-conditioned penalties, user-specified length constraints, and stage-dependent overlength filtering.
routes.inference_token_connection: Direct: explicitly optimizes or constrains response length while attempting to preserve accuracy; this is the survey's clearest token-efficiency route.
routes.notes: The survey says the principled cost-performance trade-off remains open and warns about both overthinking and underthinking.

routes.problem: A fixed long context budget makes early RL unstable and encourages unnecessarily long solutions.
routes.mechanism: Staged context lengthening (for example 8k -> 16k -> 24k/32k), short-context warm-up, overlength masks/penalties, and inference-time length extrapolation.
routes.inference_token_connection: Direct/indirect: short-context training is reported to force more concise patterns; inference-time extrapolation changes maximum capacity rather than proving fewer tokens at equal accuracy.
routes.notes: This route mixes training stability with an intended inference budget effect; retain the distinction in downstream synthesis.

routes.problem: Static RL data can be low-quality, too easy/hard, or lack verifiable intermediate traces.
routes.mechanism: Shift from scale-first corpora to distilled/annotated/verified data, multi-trajectory traces, quality filtering, explicit difficulty stratification, and agent/tool trajectories.
routes.inference_token_connection: Indirect: better data/process supervision may improve reasoning at a given token budget, but the survey supplies no general proof of reduced inference length.
routes.notes: Data route is mainly sample effectiveness and verifier compatibility; do not count dataset size as token efficiency.

routes.problem: Outcome-only rewards are scalable but can be unfaithful; process rewards are informative but expensive and noisy.
routes.mechanism: Hybrid outcome/process rewards, implicit process modeling, generative PRMs, and step-level credit assignment attempt to combine scalable goals with dense guidance.
routes.inference_token_connection: Indirect: process fidelity may reduce wasted thought, but annotation/verifier overhead is training-side and the survey reports no settled inference-token result.
routes.notes: Evidence boundary is the survey's comparative characterization, not an independently verified benchmark result.

candidates.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
candidates.route: verifiable outcome/format reward and long-CoT RLVR
candidates.reason: Survey anchor for rule-based accuracy/format rewards, GRPO, emergent long reasoning, and the train-time/test-time compute distinction; not a direct concise-inference method.

candidates.title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
candidates.reason: Introduces the group-baseline critic-free route used by later LRM RL; the survey links it to variance reduction, not lower inference token count.

candidates.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
candidates.reason: Survey credits DAPO with oversampling/filtering saturated or degenerate prompts, non-zero-advantage batches, and length-related reward handling; rollout efficiency is training-side.

candidates.title: Let's Verify Step by Step
candidates.route: process reward model and step-level credit
candidates.reason: Survey uses it as the canonical comparison where process supervision gives denser, more stable guidance than outcome-only reward, with annotation-cost caveats.

candidates.title: PRIME: Process Reinforcement through Implicit Rewards
candidates.route: implicit token-level process reward and online filtering
candidates.reason: Survey describes implicit token rewards from ORM learning and filtering of too-easy/too-hard prompts; any inference-token benefit is not established.

candidates.title: Stop Summation: Min-Form Credit Assignment Is All Process Reward Model Needs for Reasoning
candidates.reason: A concrete credit-allocation alternative intended to reduce process-reward hacking; the survey frames it as training optimization, not inference compression.

candidates.title: Segment Policy Optimization: Effective Segment-Level Credit Assignment in RL for Large Language Models
candidates.reason: Survey groups SPO with tree/shared-prefix methods for finer process rewards and sample reuse; this is RL rollout efficiency and may increase search computation.

candidates.title: TreePO: Bridging the Gap of Policy Optimization and Efficacy and Inference Efficiency with Heuristic Tree-Based Modeling
candidates.reason: The survey reports reduced training GPU hours and improved sampling efficiency through segment-wise trees; title suggests inference efficiency but the survey evidence read here is primarily training-side.

candidates.title: Improving Data Efficiency for LLM Reinforcement Fine-Tuning through Difficulty-Targeted Online Data Selection and Rollout Replay
candidates.reason: Representative data/rollout efficiency route: allocate training samples to informative difficulty regions and replay useful rollouts.

candidates.title: Learn to Reason Efficiently with Adaptive Length-Based Reward Shaping
candidates.reason: Explicitly targets efficient reasoning by conditioning length penalties/rewards on difficulty; one of the survey's direct inference-token candidates, although the survey does not independently validate its Pareto curve.

candidates.title: Efficient RL Training for Reasoning Models via Length-Aware Optimization
candidates.reason: Survey identifies it as a direct length-control route that seeks to reduce reasoning cost while retaining accuracy; evidence boundary remains survey-level.

candidates.title: Sample More to Think Less: Group Filtered Policy Optimization for Concise Reasoning
candidates.route: concise reasoning via group-filtered policy optimization
candidates.reason: The survey reports reduced redundant reasoning and 35-61% shorter sequences with slight accuracy improvements; this is the strongest explicit direct token-efficiency evidence mentioned in the survey, but remains a cited claim not independently checked here.

candidates.title: Pass@k Training for Adaptively Balancing Exploration and Exploitation of Large Reasoning Models
candidates.reason: Directly decomposes set-level Pass@K targets into sample credit and addresses exploration/exploitation; relevance is candidate quality/diversity at a budget, not fewer tokens per answer.

gaps_conflicts: The survey's taxonomy is organized around reward design, policy optimization, and sampling, not around an explicit inference-token Pareto frontier. Direct token-efficiency routes are concentrated in Sections 3.2.5, 3.3.2, and 7.4.
Training rollout throughput/sample efficiency, KV-cache reuse, asynchronous infrastructure, and lower GPU hours are repeatedly discussed but must not be reported as lower final reasoning-token usage.

Outcome rewards are scalable and verifiable but may reward unfaithful or hacked chains; process rewards improve credit assignment but require costly/noisy labels or online PRM computation. The survey does not resolve the trade-off.
Pass@1 versus Pass@K evidence is explicitly conflicting: RL can sharpen single-sample success while reducing diversity; later self-play/Pass@K objectives reopen the discovery view.

Length control has a two-sided failure mode: overthinking when unconstrained and underthinking/premature halting when aggressively truncated. The survey states that a principled marginal-utility cost-performance policy remains unsolved.
The fixed source is arXiv v3 dated 2025-10-09. It includes some September 2025 citations/models, but it is not a 2026 survey; no post-v3 updates were covered.
